title: Define blended cost per 1M output tokens (finance-aligned) + reconciliation process
creator: Talia Benson
description:
Background
We need a single, finance-aligned definition of the dashboard headline metric: blended $/1M output tokens. This metric will be used for (a) internal executive reporting, (b) prioritizing runtime/infra optimization work, and (c) explaining cost drivers across model/region/tier.

This ticket finalizes:
1) the metric definition (numerator + denominator + dimensions)
2) inclusion/exclusion rules
3) reconciliation approach vs Finance totals and vs billing
4) sign-off checklist and versioning policy

Proposed metric name (canonical)
- blended_cost_usd_per_1m_output_tokens_v1

Definition (v1)
Blended $/1M output tokens = (Allocated inference COGS in USD / Attributed output tokens) * 1,000,000

Denominator (Attributed output tokens)
- Source: platform token metering (gateway/runtime metering pipeline)
- Definition: output tokens actually generated by Redwood models (post any truncation), inclusive of streaming and non-streaming paths
- Granularity for aggregation: hourly buckets (UTC), by canonical dimensions
- Dimensions required for v1 headline + drilldowns:
  - model_id (canonical) + model_version (semver-ish or build id)
  - quantization_profile (allowed values list; "unknown" permitted)
  - region (canonical mapping table; "unknown" permitted)
  - customer_tier (self_serve | dedicated | private | enterprise; "unknown" permitted)
- Inclusion:
  - chat completions / text generation
  - tool/function calling output tokens that are produced by the model (tool arguments)
- Exclusion (v1):
  - embeddings tokens (separate metric family)
  - reranking tokens (separate metric family)
  - prompt/input tokens (tracked, but not in denominator of headline metric)

Numerator (Allocated inference COGS in USD)
Allocated inference COGS is computed for the same time window and dimensions as the denominator, with allocation rules in ADR-034.

v1 cost components included (numerator)
- GPU compute (hosted + dedicated + private where metered by Redwood):
  - hourly GPU cost rate by region/provider/capacity class from Finance rate card
  - includes reserved/on-demand blended rate per Finance methodology
- GPU-related platform overheads allocated as "Inference Shared Overhead" (if Finance includes these in infra COGS):
  - cluster control plane infra
  - networking/egress where material and attributable
  - monitoring/logging infra (only if included in Finance’s COGS bundle)

v1 cost components excluded (numerator)
- R&D payroll
- Sales/CS tooling
- Customer success labor
- One-time non-recurring credits/promotions (these affect revenue, not COGS)

Idle capacity treatment (decision required)
We will follow ADR-034 and Finance methodology:
- Hosted and autoscaled pools: idle allocation included implicitly via blended hourly GPU rates at fleet level (i.e., effective cost per GPU-hour already captures utilization)
- Dedicated reserved pools:
  - Idle is included in numerator for the dedicated tier (cost follows reservation), allocated to dedicated customer_tier regardless of actual token volume
  - Allocation basis within tier is output tokens (so low-usage dedicated customers may show higher blended cost, which is expected)
- Private deployments:
  - For Redwood-managed private in customer VPC: cost is allocated to private tier based on GPU-hours and output tokens; if customer supplies hardware (on-prem), COGS is not included unless Finance provides a chargeback rate (v1: exclude on-prem customer-owned hardware; show "N/A" cost or separate reporting class)

Allocation basis (within a cost pool)
- Primary: output tokens (because headline metric is $/output token)
- Secondary/guardrails:
  - if output_tokens == 0 for a bucket but cost exists, bucket remains but metric is flagged; do not drop rows silently

FX and currency
- All computations in USD
- If upstream rate card sources include non-USD, Finance provides normalized USD rates; pipeline should not do FX conversions ad hoc

Time boundaries
- Storage/aggregation in UTC; Finance reporting views may re-bucket to Pacific Time for exec packs
- Reconciliation reports must specify time zone explicitly (default UTC) to avoid day-boundary drift

Versioning policy (v1)
- Metric definition versioned as v1, with a Confluence metric dictionary entry as source of truth
- Rate card versioned by quarter (e.g., 2025Q4) and stored with effective_start/effective_end; dashboard should display rate_card_version used for the selected time range
- If definition changes (e.g., idle allocation rules), bump to v2 and keep v1 available for historical comparability

Reconciliation approach
We need two reconciliations:
A) Dashboard metric vs Finance infra COGS inputs
- Goal: for a chosen month/quarter, total allocated inference COGS in warehouse must match Finance-provided inference COGS (within agreed tolerance)
- Tolerance target: <= 1.5% monthly variance after known exclusions
- Method:
  1) Finance provides monthly inference COGS by region/provider/capacity class (and any overhead bundles)
  2) Aggregation job allocates to dimensions; we compute a rollup that re-aggregates back to Finance’s categories
  3) Compare totals; document known reasons for residuals (timing, late invoices, adjustments)

B) Dashboard metric vs billing totals (usage metering parity)
- Goal: output token counts by customer_tier and model should be consistent with billing usage (for hosted/self-serve) and internal contract reporting (for dedicated/private)
- We do NOT expect COGS to reconcile to customer invoices (pricing != cost)
- What must reconcile:
  - Output token metering totals for hosted/self-serve by day should match billing usage totals within 0.5% after excluding refunds/voided invoices

Sign-off deliverables
- Updated metric dictionary entry in Confluence
- Finance methodology note (or explicit endorsement) of numerator components + idle treatment
- Reconciliation report view with documented tolerances and known limitations
- Engineering acknowledgment of streaming parity + dimension completeness SLOs

- Finance methodology: sources/confluence/finance-and-legal/budgeting-and-forecasting/blended-cost-methodology-v1.json
- Kickoff notes: sources/google_drive/shared_drives/engineering/observability/unit-economics-dashboard-kickoff-notes.json

- Slack thread (definition alignment): sources/slack/eng-platform/1737332112-unit-econ-metric-definition-alignment.json
- Finance email signoff: sources/gmail/laura_bennett/20250121-unit-economics-metric-definition-signoff.json

Open decisions (must close before v1 launch)
1) Dedicated idle allocation: confirm "idle stays in dedicated tier" (Finance preference) vs reallocation to hosted (rejected in ADR draft).
2) On-prem private: confirm v1 handling as "excluded from COGS" unless Finance provides chargeback rates.
3) Overhead bundle: which shared overhead line items are included in inference COGS for this KPI (Finance to enumerate).
4) Rounding + presentation: how many decimals and how to handle low-volume buckets (Design ticket DES-319 references formatting).

Acceptance criteria
- Confluence metric dictionary updated and explicitly references v1 definition and rate card versioning.
- Laura Bennett (CFO) + Rishi Malhotra (FP&A) sign off in writing on:
  - numerator components and idle treatment
  - reconciliation tolerance + cadence
- Engineering confirms output token denominator parity across streaming and non-streaming (ENG-8421) and that "unknown" dimension buckets are retained (no silent drops).
- Reconciliation report spec is unblocked for implementation (ENG-8430): required breakdown dimensions and time zone conventions agreed.

Sign-off checklist (use for go/no-go)
- [ ] Finance-approved numerator line items list published (link)
- [ ] Finance rate card provenance and quarterly update cadence documented
- [ ] Idle capacity treatment documented and aligns with ADR-034
- [ ] Denominator definition includes streaming paths + tool calling outputs
- [ ] Unknown/missing dimensions retained and surfaced in dashboard confidence indicators
- [ ] Monthly reconciliation query/view exists and is reviewed by Finance (sample month)
- [ ] Billing usage parity check exists for hosted tokens (sample week)
- [ ] Versioning policy approved (v1 frozen; v2 process defined)
comments: 2025-01-17 (Talia Benson): Drafted v1 definition proposal based on kickoff. Main unresolved items: dedicated idle treatment + on-prem private COGS handling. Looping in Laura/Rishi for signoff target by end of month.

2025-01-21 (Rishi Malhotra): Confirmed Finance preference: dedicated reservations carry idle and should remain in dedicated tier; do not smear across hosted. Also want rate card version surfaced in UI for auditability (Q4 rate card as default).

2025-01-24 (Nadia Rahman): Denominator risks: streaming output tokens still undercount on one code path; ENG-8421 in progress. Proposed that we keep "unknown" region/model buckets rather than dropping rows, so cost/token spikes are visible as data quality issues.

2025-01-28 (Marissa Cole): Added explicit separation between COGS reconciliation and billing reconciliation (tokens only). Finance asked for a standard "Finance View" time zone bucketing (PT) in the reconciliation report to match exec pack conventions.

2025-02-03 (Laura Bennett): Approved numerator scope contingent on overhead bundle list being explicit (what’s included/excluded). Agreed on monthly tolerance <= 1.5% variance after adjustments; any larger variance requires incident + explanation in KPI pack notes.

2025-02-07 (Dylan Brooks): Engineering agreed to treat on-prem customer-owned hardware as excluded for v1 COGS (report as N/A or separate class) to avoid mixing accounting assumptions. Will revisit once we have a consistent chargeback model.

2025-02-11 (Talia Benson): Marking as Done. Finance signoff captured in email thread; Confluence metric dictionary updated to reference v1 and rate card versioning. Remaining work is implementation tickets (ENG-8430 reconciliation report + SLOs).
